actions.name: get_sources_by_target
actions.description:
Get sources by target. Returns a list of source objects whose values are populated with the id of a related target object.  For example,
if you have a lookup field called "Success Manager" on a ticket, this endpoint can answer the question,
"What tickets (sources) is this user (found by `target_type` and `target_id`)
assigned as the 'Success Manager' (field referenced by `field_id`)?"

This endpoint also resolves [multi-lookup fields](/api-reference/ticketing/lookup_relationships/lookup_relationships/#about-multi-lookup-relationship-fields).
Pass the multi-lookup field's id as `field_id` and "zen:ticket" as `source_type` to list the tickets that
reference a target record through the field...

target_type.description:
The type of object the relationship field is targeting.
The options are "zen:user", "zen:ticket", "zen:organization", and "zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY"

target_id.description: The id of the object the relationship field is targeting

field_id.description: The id of the lookup relationship field

source_type.description:
The type of object the relationship field belongs to (example. ticket field belongs to a ticket object).
The options are "zen:user", "zen:ticket", "zen:organization", and "zen:custom_object:CUSTOM_OBJECT_KEY"

actions.name: show_email_settings
actions.description:
Show Email Settings. Returns the email settings for the account.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with extensions_and_channel_management permission

actions.name: update_email_settings
actions.description:
Update Email Settings. Updates email settings for the account.

#### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with extensions_and_channel_management permission

email_category_outcome_overrides.description: Whether emails that match given categories follow the default outcome or experience overrides to accept or suspend. Only present when the feature is available for the account.

email_hc_ai_agent_comments.description: Whether AI agent comments are included in email notifications for Help Center tickets. Only present when the feature is available for the account.

email_sender_authentication.description: Whether incoming email is subjected to sender authentication checks (SPF, DKIM). This setting is deprecated and will be removed soon. It can still be turned on, but after it's on you can't turn it off

email_sender_authentication_profile.description: The sender authentication profile in use.

email_status.description: Whether email status and delivery information is shown in the Agent Workspace

email_voice_ai_agent_comments.description: Whether AI agent comments are included in email notifications for voice tickets. Only present when the feature is available for the account.

gmail_fallback_enabled.description: Whether Gmail messages that cannot be delivered via Gmail are retried via SMTP

multi_recipient_email_tickets.description: Whether a separate ticket is created for each support address that receives the same inbound email. [Learn about multi-recipient email tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10584454777370)

actions.name: get_account_settings
actions.description:
Show Settings. Shows the settings that are available for the account.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

authenticity_token.description: Legacy CSRF token. Ignored by API.

actions.name: update_zendesk_account_settings
actions.description:
Update Account Settings. Updates settings for the account. See [JSON Format](#json-format) above for the settings you can update.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

access_logs_enabled.description:
Only takes effect for accounts with at least one Advanced Data Protection
SKU product; otherwise silently dropped before the setting is saved
(`settings_controller_support.rb`, `products.none?(&:advanced_data_protection_sku?)`).

approvals_activated.description:
Rejected with a 422 ("Approvals cannot be activated for this account") unless
the account has `has_activate_approvals?` (`validate_approvals_settings`,
`settings_controller.rb`). Setting it to `true` also activates approval-related
views and object triggers as a side effect.

approvers_as_end_users.description:
Rejected with a 422 unless the account has `has_activate_approvals?`
(`validate_end_user_approvers`, `settings_controller.rb`).

active_features.description:
Feature toggles for the account. See `Zendesk::Accounts::SettingsControllerSupport`
(`args_transformation_map['active_features']`), `app/controllers/api/v2/account/settings_controller.rb`.

agent_workspace.description:
May be silently dropped without effect in either direction
(`validate_agent_workspace_update`, `settings_controller_support.rb`):
turning it on is dropped unless the account is `agent_workspace_compatible?`
and has `aw_self_serve_migration_enabled`, and (if Groups & Departments
aren't migrated) dropped outright when the account has a Chat product,
otherwise `groups.check_group_name_uniqueness` is forced to `true` as a side
effect; turning it off is dropped if the account has native messaging or
`aw_prevent_opt_out` without the auto-activation override. Setting it to
`false` also forces `routing.enabled` to `false`
(`settings_controller_support.rb:481-483`).

idle_timeout_enabled.description:
Deprecated: silently dropped without effect for accounts with the
`deprecate_idle_timeout_from_settings_api` Arturo
(`has_deprecate_idle_timeout_from_settings_api?`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`).

show_user_profile_page_toggle.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has
`has_ocp_customer_profile?` (`settings_controller_support.rb`).

split_view_enabled.description:
Writing this also writes the canonical EAP setting
`split_view_eap_enabled` to the same value unless
`split_view_eap_enabled` itself is explicitly set in the same request
(`synchronize_split_view_eap_settings`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`).

split_view_tos_accepted.description:
Writing this also writes the canonical EAP setting
`split_view_eap_tos_accepted` to the same value unless
`split_view_eap_tos_accepted` itself is explicitly set in the same request
(`synchronize_split_view_eap_settings`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`).

suggested_assignees_group_ids.description:
Each id must be a positive integer (`Parameters.gt(0)`). Duplicates are
removed before persistence (`settings_controller_support.rb`).

unified_agent_statuses.description:
For accounts with `has_omnichannel_contact_centre_enabled?`, this is
overwritten to match `routing.enabled` whenever `routing.enabled` is
present in the same request — even if this request does not otherwise
touch `agents` (`sync_routing_and_unified_agent_statuses`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`).

agents.description:
See the authorization note on the parent object: a non-admin agent may
only send this key when every property in it is one of
`spell_checker_enabled`, `ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled` or
`ai_translation_disclosure_enabled`.

macro_content_suggestions_title_gen_enab.description:
Restricted to the account owner: the controller attaches `current_user` to
this setting's record so its validation can check ownership
(`ACCT_OWNER_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

accepted_api_agreement.description:
Can only be accepted, never revoked — the controller declares this parameter
as `Parameters.enum(true)`, so `false` is rejected at the gate
(`settings_controller.rb`).

api_password_access.description:
Coupled to two-step verification enforcement as a side effect: disabling
this while 2SV enforcement is on turns 2SV enforcement off, and enabling it
while 2SV enforcement is off turns 2SV enforcement on
(`update_two_step_verification_enforce`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

slack_workspace.description: Slack workspace identifier for the Approvals Slack integration.

threshold.description:
Must resolve via `Zendesk::Types::PredictionThresholdType.find`; a value
that does not resolve is silently ignored rather than rejected
(`update_automatic_answers_settings`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

automatic_answers.description:
Automatic Answers settings. See `update_automatic_answers_settings`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`. Unlike every other category, this one is not
in `args_transformation_map` — it is special-cased directly in
`normalize_and_update_settings`.

header_color.description:
6-character hex color, no leading `#` (`Branding.validate`). Omitted or
invalid ⇒ reset to the hardcoded default `03363D`, not left unchanged. See
the destructive-partial note on the parent object.

page_background_color.description:
6-character hex color, no leading `#`. Omitted or invalid ⇒ reset to the
hardcoded default `333333`, not left unchanged. See the destructive-partial
note on the parent object.

tab_background_color.description:
6-character hex color, no leading `#`. Omitted or invalid ⇒ reset to the
hardcoded default `7FA239`, not left unchanged. See the destructive-partial
note on the parent object.

text_color.description:
6-character hex color, no leading `#`. Omitted or invalid ⇒ reset to the
hardcoded default `FFFFFF`, not left unchanged. See the destructive-partial
note on the parent object.

branding.description:
Branding colors. See `Branding.from_hash` (`lib/branding.rb`), invoked from
`settings_controller_support.rb` as
`current_account.branding = Branding.from_hash(setting_arguments['branding'])`.

**Destructive partial**: `Branding.from_hash` builds a brand-new `Branding`
instance seeded with hardcoded defaults (`03363D` / `7FA239` / `FFFFFF` /
`333333`), then overwrites only the keys present and valid in this payload — it
does not start from the account's current branding. Any property omitted from
this object, or supplied with an invalid value (must be a 6-character hex
string), is silently reset to that hardcoded default rather than left
unchanged. Sending only one color resets the other three.

**Two `Branding` attributes are not exposed here at all**: `tab_hover_color`
(default `ACC76B`) and `sidebox_color` (default `F6F6F6`) exist on the model
(`lib/branding.rb`) but have no corresponding key in this endpoint's parameter
gate (`settings_controller.rb`). Because `Branding.from_hash` always
constructs a fresh instance rather than seeding from the account's current
branding, **any request that includes a `branding` key at all unconditionally
resets both of these to their hardcoded defaults** — there is no way to
preserve the account's current `tab_hover_color`/`sidebox_color` through this
endpoint. This is pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this change; flagged
here so a caller reading this schema isn't surprised by it.

brand_user_separation_scope_query_defaul.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has
`has_brand_user_separation_scope_query_param?`
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

email_category_outcome_overrides.description: Whether emails that match given categories follow the default outcome or experience overrides to accept or suspend. Only present when the feature is available for the account.

email_hc_ai_agent_comments.description:
Deleted from the request before processing unless the account has
`has_email_ai_agent_comment_notifications?` (`settings_controller.rb#update`).

email_voice_ai_agent_comments.description:
Deleted from the request before processing unless the account has
`has_email_voice_ai_agent_comment_notifications?`
(`settings_controller.rb#update`).

html_mail_template.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has
`allow_email_template_customization?` (`settings_controller_support.rb`).

mail_delimiter.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has
`allow_email_template_customization?` (`settings_controller_support.rb`).

text_mail_template.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has
`allow_email_template_customization?` (`settings_controller_support.rb`).

check_group_name_uniqueness.description:
Also written as a side effect of `agents.agent_workspace`: enabling Agent
Workspace when Groups & Departments aren't yet migrated and the account has
no Chat product forces this to `true`
(`validate_agent_workspace_update`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

universal_import_enabled.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has the
`itam_universal_import` Arturo — the key is only registered in the write
map when that Arturo is enabled
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

default_locale_identifier.description:
Must resolve via `TranslationLocale.find_by_locale`; a value that does not
resolve to a known locale is silently ignored rather than rejected
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

localization.description:
Localization settings. See `settings_controller_support.rb`
(`args_transformation_map['localization']` and the `default_locale_identifier`
special case).

messaging_end_session.description:
Setting this to `false` also forces `routing.transform_to_email_enabled` to
`false` in the same request (`settings_controller_support.rb:485-487`), and
is itself required (this request's value, or the account's existing
setting) for `routing.transform_to_email_enabled` to be enabled
(`validate_assignment_setting_set`, `settings_controller.rb`).

messaging_ticket_subject_template.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has
`has_permissions_data_masking_adpp?` — the controller only registers this
key in its write map for accounts with that capability
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

reminders.description:
At most 3 reminders. Tags on each reminder are lower-cased, split on commas
and whitespace, deduplicated and compacted before validation
(`sanitize_tags`, `settings_controller.rb`). Then validated positionally by
`MessagingInactivityValidator` — the array's index, not any field on the
item, decides which fields are required: the first reminder (index 0) must
omit both `timeout` and `ticket_status_id`; the second (index 1) must
supply `timeout`; the third (index 2) must supply both `timeout` and a
non-null `ticket_status_id`. A validation failure on any reminder renders a
400 for the whole request.

items.description:
See the positional requirements on the parent `reminders` array — which
fields are required depends on this item's position in the array, not on
the item's own contents. `message` is the one exception: it is required
at every position — the gate declares it `Parameters.string.required`,
so a reminder without a `message` is rejected with a 400 before the
positional validator runs.

ticket_status_id.description:
The only property in this entire payload where an explicit `null` is
genuinely accepted: the controller declares this parameter
as `Parameters.integer | Parameters.nil` in the gate itself
(`settings_controller.rb`), which is unaffected by the action's
`forbid_nil_parameters` opt-in — that opt-in only disables the
process-wide `allow_nil_for_everything` short-circuit, not an
explicit `| Parameters.nil` declared on this one field. Null (or
omission) is accepted for reminders at index 0 or 1; a reminder at
index 2 that has a null or missing `ticket_status_id` fails
`MessagingInactivityValidator`'s presence check with a 400.

timeout.description:
Seconds (note: the top-level `timeout` sibling is minutes). Enforced
at the parameter gate as `60..900`.
Minutes. Enforced at the parameter gate as `3..15`.

messaging_inactivity.description:
Messaging inactivity (capacity release) settings. See
`settings_controller_support.rb` (`args_transformation_map['messaging_inactivity']`),
`app/validators/messaging_inactivity_validator.rb`, and
`settings_controller.rb#update`.

idle_timeout.description: Minutes. Enforced at the parameter gate as `10..120`.

pull.description:
Flattened before persistence: `limit_concurrent_chats` is written to the
`messaging_routing_pull_limit_concurrent_chats` account setting
(`flatten_messaging_routing_settings`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

push.description:
Flattened before persistence: `limit_concurrent_chats` is written to the
`messaging_routing_push_limit_concurrent_chats` account setting
(`flatten_messaging_routing_settings`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

messaging_routing.description:
The whole key is deleted from the request without effect unless the
account has `messaging_routing_enabled` (`has_messaging_routing_enabled?`,
`settings_controller.rb`).

notifications_preference_admin_setting.description:
The entire `notifications` object is deleted from the request before
processing unless the account has the `admin_center_framework_api_notifications_setting`
Arturo — the same one gating the Admin Center notifications settings UI
(`settings_controller.rb#update`).

notifications.description:
The whole object is dropped without effect unless the account has the
`admin_center_framework_api_notifications_setting` Arturo — see
`AccountSettingsNotificationsInput.yaml`.

onboarding_segments.description:
Sanitized before saving: split on commas, deduplicated, and intersected
with `Users::OnboardingSupport::SEGMENTS` — unrecognized segments are
silently dropped (`sanitize_onboarding_segments`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`).

enabled.description:
For accounts with `has_omnichannel_contact_centre_enabled?`, sending this
also overwrites `agents.unified_agent_statuses` to the same value, even if
this request does not otherwise touch `agents`
(`sync_routing_and_unified_agent_statuses`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

missed_messaging_assignments.description:
Both this key and `missed_talk_assignments` are dropped from the request
before any validation or processing unless the account has the
`ocr_missed_assignments_limit` Arturo
(`has_ocr_missed_assignments_limit?`, `settings_controller.rb`). Unlike
every other property in this payload, only the keys supplied here are
written — they are merged into the account's existing stored
`routing_missed_messaging_assignments` hash, so omitted keys keep their
stored values (`merge_missed_assignments_settings`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`).

missed_talk_assignments.description:
Dropped from the request before any validation or processing unless the
account has the `ocr_missed_assignments_limit` Arturo
(`has_ocr_missed_assignments_limit?`, `settings_controller.rb`) — see
`missed_messaging_assignments` for the merge-into-stored-hash semantics.

throttle_cool_down_time.description:
Validated to 30-720; an out-of-range update fails the save
(`register_property :routing_throttle_cool_down_time`,
`app/models/account_setting.rb`).

throttle_percentage_email.description:
Validated to 1-99; an out-of-range update fails the save
(`register_property :routing_throttle_percentage_email`,
`app/models/account_setting.rb`).

throttle_percentage_messaging.description:
Validated to 1-99; an out-of-range update fails the save
(`register_property :routing_throttle_percentage_messaging`,
`app/models/account_setting.rb`).

throttle_ramp_up_time_email.description:
Validated to 5-180; an out-of-range update fails the save
(`register_property :routing_throttle_ramp_up_time_email`,
`app/models/account_setting.rb`).

throttle_ramp_up_time_messaging.description:
Validated to 5-180; an out-of-range update fails the save
(`register_property :routing_throttle_ramp_up_time_messaging`,
`app/models/account_setting.rb`).

transform_to_email_enabled.description:
Rejected with a 422 unless `messaging.messaging_end_session` (this
request's value, or the account's existing
`messaging_end_session_enabled` setting) is enabled
(`validate_assignment_setting_set`, `settings_controller.rb`). Also forced
to `false` as a side effect whenever `messaging.messaging_end_session` is
explicitly set to `false` in the same request
(`settings_controller_support.rb:485-487`).

enable_macro_suggestions.description:
Silently dropped without effect unless the account has
`has_macro_suggestions?` — the feature is still in EAP
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

skill_based_filtered_views.description:
Only one view can be a skill-filtered view today: an array with more than
one element is silently discarded (not clamped, not rejected) rather than
saved, and a single value (or single-element array) is normalized and
stored as a one-element array (`settings_controller_support.rb`).

saas_management_enabled.description:
Top-level setting, not nested under a category
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

agent_email_ccs_become_followers.description:
Forced to `false` whenever `comment_email_ccs_allowed` is explicitly set to
`false` in the same request, overriding any other value sent for this
property in that request (`settings_controller_support.rb:383-386`).

attachment_otp.description:
Silently dropped without effect, together with `attachment_otp_duration`,
unless the account has the `attachment_otp_challenge` capability
(`has_attachment_otp_challenge?`, `settings_controller_support.rb`).

attachment_otp_duration.description:
Silently dropped without effect, together with `attachment_otp`, unless the
account has the `attachment_otp_challenge` capability
(`has_attachment_otp_challenge?`, `settings_controller_support.rb`). The
saved value is validated to 1-720 (`register_property
:attachment_otp_duration`, `app/models/account_setting.rb`); an out-of-range
update fails the save.

auto_updated_ccs_followers_rules.description:
Sending `false` is a no-op: the key is dropped before persisting unless
truthy (`acct_settings.delete('auto_updated_ccs_followers_rules') unless
acct_settings['auto_updated_ccs_followers_rules']`,
`settings_controller_support.rb`), so this setting can be turned on via this
endpoint but not turned off.

cc_email_template.description:
Only takes effect when `new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — see
`collaboration` above.

cc_subject_template.description:
Only takes effect when `new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — see
`collaboration` above.

collaboration.description:
Only takes effect for accounts where new-collaboration is disabled, i.e.
`new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — the account has neither
`has_follower_and_email_cc_collaborations_enabled?` nor accepted the
new-collaboration EAP ToS (`settings_controller_support.rb`). Accepted at
the gate regardless of account state; silently has no effect otherwise.

collaborators_addable_only_by_agents.description:
Only takes effect when `new_collaboration_disabled?` is true — see
`collaboration` above.

comment_email_ccs_allowed.description:
Setting this to `false` also forces `agent_email_ccs_become_followers` and
`light_agent_email_ccs_allowed` to `false` in the same request, even if this
request explicitly supplies a different value for either of them
(`settings_controller_support.rb:383-386`).

edit_ticket_skills_permission.description:
Any integer is accepted at the gate, but only `0`-`3` are meaningful
(`EDITABLE_BY_ADMINS`/`VISIBLE_TO_AGENTS`/`HIDDEN_FOR_ALL`/`EDITABLE_BY_ALL`).
Any other value is silently coerced to `0` before being saved
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

light_agent_email_ccs_allowed.description:
Forced to `false` whenever `comment_email_ccs_allowed` is explicitly set to
`false` in the same request, overriding any other value sent for this
property in that request (`settings_controller_support.rb:383-386`).

only_allowed_attachment_file_types.description:
When set to the string `custom`, `custom_allowed_attachment_file_types_list`
(this request's value, or the account's existing one) must be non-blank or
the update raises (`settings_controller_support.rb`).

push_solved_ticket_reassignment_strategy.description:
Not stored as a setting: a truthy value enqueues a one-off
`GroupDefaultReassignmentStrategyJob`, throttled per-account
(`settings_controller_support.rb`).

suspended_ticket_notification.description:
Merged (not replaced) onto the account's existing suspended-ticket
notification record via `ActiveRecord#update`
(`update_suspended_notification`, `settings_controller_support.rb`), so
omitted keys are left unchanged rather than cleared.

ticket_id_sequence.description:
Only takes effect when it parses to an integer greater than the account's
current ticket-id sequence position; otherwise silently ignored
(`update_ticket_id_sequence`, `settings_controller_support.rb`). Cannot lower
the sequence.

tickets.description:
See the authorization note on the parent object: a non-admin agent may
send this key alone (or with a restricted `agents` subset).

settings.description:
The account settings to update. Every category and property is optional — a
request only needs to include the settings it wants to change; omitted
categories and properties are left unchanged. See
`allow_parameters :update`, `app/controllers/api/v2/account/settings_controller.rb`,
and `Zendesk::Accounts::SettingsControllerSupport.normalize_and_update_settings`,
`lib/zendesk/accounts/settings_controller_support.rb`, for the full trace.

A non-admin agent may only update this object when it is either `{"tickets": ...}`
alone, or `{"agents": ...}` (or both `agents` and `tickets`) where every `agents`
key is one of `spell_checker_enabled`, `ai_async_comment_translations_eap_enabled`
or `ai_translation_disclosure_enabled` — any other combination of top-level keys
requires full admin (`conditional_require_permission_or_admin!`/
`tickets_settings_payload?`, `settings_controller.rb`). This authorization rule
ranges over the whole request body, not any single property, and cannot be
expressed as a schema constraint here — see the property descriptions on
`agents`/`tickets` instead.

actions.name: create_trial_account
actions.description: Create Trial Account.

_zd_choose_shard_udupi.description: Preferred database shard for the new account. Formerly read by `Zendesk::Accounts::Initializer` on the Classic creation path, which PLATOPS-1372 removed; the value is now accepted and forwarded verbatim, and whether the account service honours it is outside this repository.

employee_service_suite_trial.description: Provisions an Employee Service Suite trial (a professional-plan `employee_service_suite` SKU expiring in 14 days) with `account.account_type` set to `pre_spp`. Enabled by any value the parameter gate coerces to true (`1`, `"1"`, `true`, `"true"`, `"on"`). Takes effect only when `zendesk_suite_trial` is not set, which is evaluated first.

google_apps_domain.description: Google Workspace domain to associate with the account. Must not already be routed to another account and must not be `gmail.com`; either returns `409 Conflict`.

help_desk_size.description: Free-form description of the expected number of agents, for example `Small Team`, `1-9` or `Large group`. Surfaced verbatim as `company_size` in the signup tracking properties (`Account::Tracking`); any categorisation happens downstream of this repository. Not enforced by this controller's own gates; `Account` validates its presence on create, but the record is created by the account service, out of process. `null` and omission are indistinguishable here.

language.description: Locale for the new account, for example `ja`. Copied to `account.locale` before the payload is forwarded.

multiproduct.description: Legacy switch for the account's product configuration. PLATOPS-1372 removed the multiproduct branch and the legacy Classic fallback from `create`, so this controller no longer reads the value and it has no effect on which service handles the request. It is still accepted by the parameter gate and forwarded verbatim to the account service like every other permitted property; whether it affects provisioning is decided by the account service, outside this repository. The value the account service returns is echoed back as `account.multiproduct` in the response body.

name.description: The name of the account. Not enforced by this controller's own gates; accepted and forwarded to the account service, which decides whether it is required. `null` and omission are indistinguishable here.

remote_authentication.description: Single sign-on configuration for the new account. Accepted and forwarded to the account service verbatim; this controller does not read it.

anyOf.description: Single sign-on configuration for the new account. Corresponds to the `remote_authentication` member of `Api::V2::AccountsController::ACCOUNT_PARAMETER`.

fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the identity provider's signing certificate, for SAML configurations.

remote_login_url.description: The URL users are redirected to in order to sign in.

remote_logout_url.description: The URL users are redirected to after signing out.

type.description: The single sign-on protocol, for example `saml`. Not validated by this controller.

remote_login_url.description: Remote login URL for the account. Distinct from `remote_authentication.remote_login_url`; both are accepted and forwarded.

source.description: Provisioning channel this signup came from. Also copied into `trial_extras.source` when present.

subdomain.description: The subdomain to provision, and the only place this controller looks for it. A missing, blank, invalid, reserved or taken subdomain returns `409 Conflict` with a `success: false` body rather than a validation error. Note that a successful request locks the subdomain in the shared cache for 60 seconds *before* the account is created, so retrying a request that failed with a `422` returns a `409` until the lock expires.

suite_trial.description: Provisions a `suite` trial SKU instead of the default `support` SKU. Also copied into `trial_extras.suite_trial` when present. zendesk_suite_trial.description: Provisions a Zendesk Suite trial (a professional-plan `zendesk_suite` SKU expiring in 14 days) rather than the default SKU. is_verified.description: Marks the owner's email as already verified. Only the values `1` and `true` (in their string, boolean or integer spellings) count as verified; the controller normalises whatever is supplied to a boolean before forwarding it, so any other value, `null`, and omitting the property, mean unverified.

trial_extras.description: Free-form bag of trial metadata. Every value is coerced to a string, and the controller then injects `confirm_origin`, `creation_channel`, `original_remote_ip`, `region`, and copies `account.source` and `account.suite_trial` into it (`AccountsController#account_creation_params_trial_extras`). actions.name: list_whats_app_templates

List WhatsApp Templates. Returns the WhatsApp message templates synced from SunCo for the account's
WhatsApp integrations. Only templates approved by WhatsApp are synced.

Listing triggers a freshness check per integration. If local data is missing or stale, a
background sync is started and the `syncing` flag is set in the response. The list may be
incomplete while that flag is set, so poll until it clears.

* Cursor pagination (recommended)

- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)

These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

Number of records to return per page.

}

actions.name: create_dynamic_content_items
actions.description:
Create Item. Create a new content item, with one or more variants in the item's `variants` array. See [Specifying item variants](#specifying-item-variants).

The `default_locale_id` and variant `locale_id` values must be one of the locales the account has active. You can get the list with the [List Locales](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/locales/#list-locales) endpoint.

#### Allowed For

content.description:
The content of the item's default variant. Use this together with `default_locale_id` as a shorthand for creating
an item with a single variant. Required when `variants` is omitted — without it the default variant has no content
and the request is rejected. **Must not be sent together with `variants`** — the two forms are mutually
exclusive, and sending both returns a 400 `Invalid attribute` error whatever the value is.

default_locale_id.description:
The default locale of the item, which becomes the locale of its default variant. Must be one of the locales the
account has active. Required unless `variants` is supplied, in which case this value is **ignored** and the default
locale is taken from the variant whose `default` is `true`. A `null` is therefore only accepted alongside
`variants`; without `variants` it is rejected.

name.description:
The unique name of the item. Must be unique within the account, must not contain non-ASCII characters and must not
end in a hyphen. The item's `placeholder` is derived from it, and a name whose derived placeholder is already in
use is also rejected.

variants.description:
The variants to create for the item. Exactly one of them must have `default` set to `true`; if none does, the
request is rejected because the item would have no default variant. Supplying this array makes `default_locale_id`
inert, and `content` must not be sent alongside it. A `null` is treated as if the array were omitted, so the item is
created from `default_locale_id` and `content` instead; an empty array is **not** equivalent and is rejected.

than the Item Variants API does, so this schema is not interchangeable with a standalone variant request body.

content.description:
The content of the variant. Evaluated as Liquid in the `dc` namespace, so it must be valid Liquid and must not
reference the item's own placeholder. Cannot be blank.

default.description:
Whether this variant is the item's default variant. Exactly one variant in the array must set it to `true`, and the
request is rejected if none does. Only the literal `true` counts — `null` and any other value are treated as
`false`. If more than one variant sets it to `true`, only the last of them is stored as the default and the earlier
ones are silently discarded.

locale_id.description: The locale of the variant. Must be an existing locale id, and each locale may appear at most once per item.

actions.description:
Create End User Identity. Adds an identity to an end user's profile.

Supported identity types for end users:

| Type             | Example |
| ---------------- | ------- |
| email            | `{ "type" : "email", "value" : "someone@example.com" }` |
| phone_number     | `{ "type" : "phone_number", "value" : "+1 555-123-4567" }` |

#### Allowed For

* Verified end users

type[].description: Filters results by one or more identity types using the format `?type[]={type}&type[]={type}`

brand_id.description: When brand separation is enabled, associates the new identity with the specified brand.

auto_ownership.description: When true, creates the email identity as "owned", or as "shared" if another user owns the address. See [Shared email](/api-reference/ticketing/users/user_identities/#shared-email).

ownership.description: Sets the email identity to "owned" or "shared". Defaults to "owned". See [Shared email](/api-reference/ticketing/users/user_identities/#shared-email).

primary.description:
Makes the new identity the primary one. null is accepted and ignored. Only takes effect for `email` identities. For a verified
email identity (`verified: true` or `verification_method: low`) the identity becomes primary
immediately; for an unverified one the promotion is deferred - the verification email link carries
`make_primary=true`, so the identity becomes primary (and the former primary is removed) when the
recipient verifies. Ignored for non-email identity types, including `google`.

To promote an identity that already exists, use the
[Make Identity Primary](#make-identity-primary) endpoint instead.

type.description:
The type of identity to create.

Only the types listed here can be created through this endpoint. The remaining identity types
(`any_channel`, `foreign`, `sdk`, `microsoft`) are created by internal systems only, and a request
for one of them is rejected with a `400`.

`messaging` and `slack` back internal channel integrations. `slack` additionally requires the
Slack identity feature to be enabled on the account.

value.description:
The identifier for this identity. An email address for `email` and `google`, the screen name for
`twitter`, the Facebook user id for `facebook`, and an E.164 phone number for `phone_number` and
`agent_forwarding`. Phone numbers are validated unless the account has phone number validation
turned off.

verification_method.description:
The verification state to create the identity with. `low` creates a verified identity and
suppresses the verification email. Only `none` and `low` are accepted here; the higher methods
(`sso`, `embed`, `full`) are set by the corresponding authentication flows.

Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor
for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is
always created unverified and a verification email is sent.

null is accepted and treated exactly like `none`. Because this property wins over `verified`,
sending `verified: true` alongside `verification_method: null` creates an unverified identity.

verified.description:
Creates the identity already verified, equivalent to `verification_method: low`. Deprecated - use
`verification_method` instead. Ignored when `verification_method` is also sent - that property
wins. null is accepted and treated exactly like `false`.

Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor
for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is
always created unverified and a verification email is sent.

Search Assets. Returns an array of assets with values in text-based fields that match the search query.

If the query includes multiple words or numbers, it's treated as a space-separated list of search terms and assets with values matching one or more of the terms are returned. For example, `query=laptop Apple 2024` is encoded as `query=laptop%20Apple%202024` and treated as three distinct search terms: `laptop`, `Apple`, and `2024`. Every asset record with a text field containing 'laptop', 'Apple', or '2024' is returned.

If you need to search by more complex logic, use the [Filtered Search API](/api-reference/it-asset-management/assets/#filtered-search-of-assets) endpoint.

#### Paginat...

query.description: Lists the search terms, separated by a space, used to identify the asset records.

sort.description: Orders the returned records by: `name`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`. Defaults to sorting by relevance. Prepending `-` (`-name`, `-created_at`, or `-updated_at`) sorts the results in descending order by that value.

page[before].description: A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.before_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.

page[after].description: A [pagination cursor](/documentation/api-basics/pagination/paginating-through-lists-using-cursor-pagination) that tells the endpoint which page to start on. It should be a `meta.after_cursor` value from a previous request. Note: `page[before]` and `page[after]` can't be used together in the same request.

page[size].description: Specifies how many assets should be returned in the response, up to 100 assets per page.

actions.name: filtered_search_of_assets
actions.description:
Filtered Search of Assets. Returns an array of assets that meet the complex search and filter criteria. For simple searches limited to text fields, use the [Search Assets API](/api-reference/it-asset-management/assets/#search-assets) endpoint instead.

Filters can contain either an individual [comparison object](#comparison-object) or an array of [comparison objects](#comparison-object) within logical namespaces.

A filter is a JSON object that has the following properties:

| Name      | Type   | Required | Description
| --------- | ------ | -------- | -----------
| ATTRIBUTE | object | no       | A [comparison object](#comparison-object) specifying an attribute value condition to be met...

rollup_child_object.description: Roll-up fields only. The Zendesk resource name (ZRN) of the child object whose records are aggregated. Example: "zen:custom_object:order_item". The child object must have a parent-child relationship with this field's object

rollup_filter_criteria.description: Roll-up fields only. Optional filter conditions (using `all`/`any` arrays) to restrict which child records are included in the aggregation. Uses the same DSL as lookup relationship filters

relationship_target_type.description: A representation of what type of object the field references. For lookup fields, options are "zen:user", "zen:organization", "zen:ticket", "zen:article", "zen:brand", and "zen:custom_object:{key}" where key is a custom object key. For example "zen:custom_object:apartment". For parent fields, valid options are "zen:user", "zen:organization", "zen:ticket", and "zen:custom_object:{key}". Cannot be changed after creation.

required.description: If true, the field must have a value when creating or updating custom object records.

actions.name: get_macros
actions.description:
List Macros. Lists all shared and personal macros available to the current user. For admins, the API returns all macros for the account, including the personal macros of agents and other admins.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.

#### Allowed For
* Agents

include.description: A sideload to include in the response. See [Sideloads](#sideloads-2)

access.description: Filter macros by access. Possible values are "personal", "agents", "shared", or "account". The "agents" value returns all personal macros for the account's agents and is only available to admins.

active.description: Filter by active macros if true or inactive macros if false

group_id.description: Filter macros by group

only_viewable.description: If true, returns only macros that can be applied to tickets. If false, returns all macros the current user can manage. Default is false

sort_by.description: Possible values are "alphabetical", "created_at", "updated_at", "usage_1h", "usage_24h", "usage_7d", or "usage_30d". Defaults to alphabetical

sort_order.description: One of "asc" or "desc". Defaults to "asc" for alphabetical and position sort, "desc" for all others

sort.description:
Sort order for cursor pagination. Possible values are "alphabetical", "position", "created_at", or "updated_at".
Prefix with a dash (`-`) for descending order. Example: "-updated_at".
Usage-based sorts (`sort_by=usage_*`) are not supported with cursor pagination.

anyOf.description: Traditional offset pagination page number (non-negative integer)
Cursor pagination parameters (JSON:API style)

page.description:
Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination:

- Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number)
- Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before)

These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

per_page.description:
Number of records to return per page.

Note: Default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Check endpoint-specific
documentation for limits.

organization_id.description:
The ID of the organization to assign the user to, supplied at the root of the request instead of
inside `organization_membership`. It is only consulted when no `user_id` is given at the root or in
the query string; when it is consulted, `organization_membership.organization_id` is ignored.

This may equivalently be sent as an `organization_id` **query parameter**, which takes precedence
over the root of the body.

An organization must likewise be identified in **at least one of** three places — this property, the
`organization_id` query parameter, or `organization_membership.organization_id` — and a request that
names none of them is a 422. As with `user_id`, that rule is stated rather than encoded, because the
query location is not visible to a request-body schema.

The ID of the organization to assign the user to. Required **unless** an `organization_id` is
supplied at the root of the request or as a query parameter *and* no `user_id` is supplied in either
of those places, in which case that value selects the organization and this one is ignored.

Creating a membership has effects beyond the new row:

* If this is the user's first organization membership, it is created as the default, which also sets
  the user's `organization_id`, and every unclosed ticket requested by the user is reassigned to this
  organization.
* On accounts **without** the multiple organizations feature, all of the user's other organization
  memberships are **deleted**, and the user's unclosed requested tickets that belonged to those
  removed organizations move to the user's new default organization — or have their organization
  cleared, if the account has the `unset_ticket_org_when_removing_default_user_org` feature. Tickets
  the user has in other organizations are left alone.
* Returns a 422 if the user is already at the account's `max_organization_memberships_per_user` limit
  (300 by default).

user_id.description:
The ID of the user to assign to the organization. The user must belong to the same account as the
organization.

Required **unless** a `user_id` is supplied at the root of the request or as a query parameter, in
which case that value selects the user and this one is ignored.

inside `organization_membership`. When present it selects the user the membership is created for,
and `organization_membership.user_id` is ignored.

This may equivalently be sent as a `user_id` **query parameter**, which takes precedence over the
root of the body.

A user must be identified in **at least one of** three places — this property, the `user_id` query
parameter, or `organization_membership.user_id` — and a request that names none of them is a 422.

That rule is stated here rather than encoded as a schema constraint, deliberately: one of the three
legal locations is the **query string**, which lies outside the request body a body schema can see.
Any structural encoding of "at least one of" would therefore have to reject a body that names the
user nowhere — even though such a body is a legal `201` whenever the `user_id` query parameter
supplies it. Being unenforced is the lesser fault: over-strictness here would forbid calls the API
accepts.

Neither property is required, and neither is checked at the door — an item that omits or nulls either one, or that names a user or an organization outside the account, is accepted with a 200 and recorded as a `UserNotFound` or `OrganizationNotFound` failure against that item in the job results. organization_id.description: The ID of an organization

organization.description: Organization attributes to update. Every property is optional and omitting one leaves the stored value unchanged, but see the per-property notes: several properties replace the stored value wholesale rather than merging into it. An empty object is accepted and changes nothing.

details.description: Any details about the organization, such as the address. `null` clears the stored value.

domain_names.description: Domain names and email addresses to associate with this organization. Accepts either an array of values or a single string of values separated by commas, semicolons or spaces. **Destructive:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale, so every omitted domain and email is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all clear them all. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored list untouched.

external_id.description: A unique external id to associate the organization to an external record. The id is case-insensitive, so "company1" and "Company1" are considered the same. `null` or an empty string clears it; a value already used by another organization returns 422.

group_id.description: New tickets from users in this organization are automatically put in this group. `null` unassigns the group.

name.description: A unique name for the organization. Cannot contain the `|` character and must be unique within the account; a duplicate returns 422. Cannot be cleared — an empty string or `null` fails the presence validation with 422.

notes.description: Any notes you have about the organization. `null` clears the stored value for a caller with `edit` permission; for an agent restricted to `edit_notes`, `null` is ignored and the stored notes are left untouched — only a non-empty value (including an empty string) is assigned. This is the only attribute an agent restricted to `edit_notes` can change; for such an agent every other attribute here is silently ignored and the request still returns 200. `organization_fields` is the exception — it is applied for a restricted agent too, unless the account has `up_restrict_organization_field_updates` enabled.

organization_fields.description: Custom organization field values, keyed by field key. See [Custom organization fields](/api-reference/ticketing/organizations/organizations/#custom-organization-fields). Only keys matching an existing organization field take effect; unknown keys are silently ignored. Supplied keys are merged into the stored values, so omitted keys keep their value, and a `null` or blank value for a key deletes that field's stored value. `null` for the whole map is accepted and changes nothing. Requires the `user_and_organization_fields` account feature; without it the whole map is silently ignored, as it also is for agents without `edit` permission on organizations when the account has `up_restrict_organization_field_updates` enabled.

shared_comments.description: End users in this organization are able to comment on each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Only takes effect when `shared_tickets` is `true` — the model resets it to `false` whenever the organization is not sharing tickets.

shared_tickets.description: End users in this organization are able to see each other's tickets. An explicit `null` is rejected with 400. Setting this to `false` also forces `shared_comments` to `false`. Deprecated in favor of `ticket_restriction`, which takes precedence when both are sent in the same request: `shared_tickets` is then silently dropped from the request and, when the two contradict, the response carries a top-level `warnings` array saying so (this precedence behavior requires the `enable_sync_ticket_restriction` account feature). Sent on its own, it still applies: when the `enable_sync_ticket_restriction` account feature is enabled, the stored `ticket_restriction` is synchronized to `organization` for `true` or `restricted` for `false`; with the feature disabled a non-null stored `ticket_restriction` is left unchanged (a stored `null` always reads as derived from `shared_tickets`).

tags.description: The tags of the organization. Accepts either an array of tags or a single string of space-separated tags. Requires the `user_and_organization_tags` account feature; without it the value is accepted and silently ignored. **Destructive:** the supplied list replaces the stored list wholesale, so every omitted tag is deleted; `null`, an empty array and an empty string all remove every tag. Omit the property entirely to leave the stored tags untouched.

ticket_restriction.description: Which tickets end users in this organization can see. `restricted` hides each end user's tickets from the other end users in the organization; `organization` lets them see each other's tickets; `organization_and_descendants` extends that to end users in descendant organizations and requires the organization hierarchy to be enabled on the account, otherwise it is rejected with 422. Any other value is rejected with 422. `null` clears the stored restriction, which then derives from `shared_tickets`. Takes precedence over `shared_tickets` — see that property for what happens when both are sent.

or `null`

any.description: Logical OR. A ticket may match any of these conditions to enter the queue. `null` is accepted and treated as empty

or `null`

primary_groups_id.description:
The ids of the groups the queue routes to first. At least one is required for a group queue, and the field must be omitted when
`subqueues` is set. `null` is accepted and behaves as omitted: the group assignment is skipped entirely rather than applied as empty

priority.description:
The priority applied to tickets that enter the queue. Required for a group queue, and must be omitted when `subqueues` is set.

actions.name: create_zendesk_request
actions.description:
Create Request. Accepts a `request` object that sets one or more properties.

#### Allowed for

* End users
* Anonymous users (rate limit of 5 requests per hour for [trial accounts](/documentation/developer-tools/getting-started/getting-a-trial-or-sponsored-account-for-development/))

#### Additional properties

In addition to the writable request properties in the [JSON Format table](#json-format) above, you can set the following properties when creating a request.

| Name                | Type   | Mandatory | Comment
| ----------------    | -------| --------- | -------
| comment             | object | yes       | Describes the problem, incident, question, or task. See [Request comments]...

request.description:
The properties an end user may set when creating a request. A request is the end-user view of a ticket, and the set of
properties accepted here is much narrower than the one accepted by the Tickets API. Properties an end user is not
allowed to set for the account's configuration are discarded rather than rejected.

collaborators.description:
The collaborators (CCs) to set on the request, as user ids, email addresses, or objects carrying a name and an
email. Only applied when the account allows collaborators, and rejected when the request is submitted from the
help center by an account that does not allow help center collaborators. At most 48 collaborators may be sent in
one call on accounts with CCs and followers enabled, and null is ignored

email.description: The email address of the collaborator

name.description: The name to use if a user has to be created for `email`

body.description: The comment text, as Zendesk markdown. Takes precedence over `value`, but is overridden by `html_body` when both are sent. On create this becomes the request's `description`

html_body.description: The comment text as HTML. Takes precedence over both `body` and `value` whenever it is sent, and stores the comment in rich-text format

uploads.description:
One or more attachment upload tokens to attach to the comment. Blank tokens are discarded, and both a null and an
empty array are discarded entirely, leaving the comment with no new attachments. On an anonymous create the number
of attachments is capped by the account's anonymous attachment limit

value.description: A legacy alias for `body`, applied only when `body` is absent, and likewise overridden by `html_body`

comment.description:
The comment to add to the request. On Create Request the comment is mandatory and supplies the request's read-only
`description`. A comment carrying `uploads` but no text is rejected on both operations. Comments added through this
endpoint always take the publicity the account computes for the caller; an end user cannot choose it here.

custom_fields.description:
Custom field values, either as an array of objects carrying an `id` and a `value`, or as an object mapping ticket
field id to value. Values for fields the end user cannot see are discarded. Takes precedence over `fields` when
both are sent. A bare string, integer or boolean is tolerated and ignored, as is null

due_at.description: When a request of type "task" is due. Only applied when the Type field is editable by end users. Send null or an empty string to leave the request without a due date

email_ccs.description:
The email CCs to add to the request, up to 48 entries with `action: "put"` per call. On an account without CCs and
followers enabled the `put` entries are still applied, as plain collaborators; only `delete` entries need the
feature. Rejected when the request is submitted from the help center by an account that does not allow help center
collaborators. Null and an empty array both add no CCs

items.description: An email CC to add to, or remove from, a request.

action.description: "put" to add the email CC, "delete" to remove it. Defaults to "put", and any unrecognised value is also treated as "put"

user_email.description: The email address of the user to add or remove as an email CC. Used to look the user up when `user_id` is absent

user_id.description: The id of the user to add or remove as an email CC. Takes precedence over `user_email`

user_name.description: The name to use if a user has to be created for `user_email`

fields.description: An alias for `custom_fields`, accepting the same shapes with the same tolerances. Ignored when `custom_fields` is also sent, and null is ignored

metadata.description: An arbitrary object stored as custom metadata on the request's first audit. A value that is not an object, including null, is ignored

organization_id.description: The id of the organization to associate the request with. Must be one of the requester's organizations — any other value, and null, is silently replaced by the requester's default organization

priority.description: The priority of the request. Only applied when the Priority field is editable by end users. An unrecognised value, and null, leave the request without a priority

recipient.description: The original recipient email address to record on the request

requester.description: The requester of an anonymous request. Only applied when the request is created by an unauthenticated caller — for any authenticated caller the requester is the caller. Null is ignored

email.description: The email address of the anonymous requester. An existing user is matched on this address

locale.description: The locale to give a newly created requester. Takes precedence over `locale_id`

locale_id.description: The locale id to give a newly created requester. Ignored when `locale` is also sent

name.description: The name of the anonymous requester

safe_update.description: Has no effect on its own on create, but see `updated_stamp`: sending both fails the create with a 422

solved.description: Accepted for symmetry with Update Request but has no effect on create — a request has no assignee at creation, so it cannot be solved

subject.description: The subject of the request. Required when the account requires a subject on end-user requests

system_metadata.description: Client and IP information to store as system metadata on the request's first audit. Accepted from any caller but only applied for internal Zendesk services, and a null is ignored

client.description: The user agent to record against the request

ip_address.description: The IP address to record against the request

tags.description: The tags to set on the request. Null is ignored and leaves the request with no tags of its own

ticket_form_id.description: The id of the ticket form to apply. Only applied when the account has ticket forms. Sending null behaves exactly like omitting the property — the brand's default form is used

type.description: The type of the request. Only applied when the Type field is editable by end users. An unrecognised value, and null, leave the request without a type

updated_stamp.description:
Has no effect on its own — there is no earlier `updated_at` to compare against — but sending it together with
`safe_update: true` **fails the create** with a 422, because the safe-update check runs on a record that has no
stored timestamp yet. Send neither on create

via.description: The channel the request came through

anyOf.description:
Describes the channel the request came through. The channel is only recorded on the request when the account has the
agent-as-end-user anonymous via feature enabled, or when an internal Zendesk service records an LLM via; `source` is
always inspected to detect a help center submission, which changes whether collaborators may be set.

channel.description: The channel to record, either as a `via_id` or as a channel name. An unrecognised name is ignored and the request keeps its default channel

source.description: The via reference recorded against the request, for example the id of the ticket a follow-up came from. Send the help center via id here to identify a help center submission

rel.description: A relation name classifying the source

via_followup_source_id.description: The id of a closed ticket that this request follows up on. Only closed tickets are accepted; any other value, and null, is ignored

via_id.description:
The channel to record the request against. Only a small set of channels may be chosen by an API caller — any other
value, and null, records the request as created through the API. Ignored when `via_followup_source_id` is sent,
which records the request as a follow-up instead

actions.name: update_zendesk_requests
actions.description:
Update Request. Updates a request with a comment or collaborators (cc's). The end user who created the request can also use it to mark the request as solved. The endpoint can't be used to update other request attributes.

#### Writable properties
This endpoint can only update the following properties in the request.

| Name                     | Type    | Required | Description                                          |
| ------------------------ | ------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| comment                  | object  | no       | Adds a comment to the request. See [Request comments](#request-comments) |
| solved                   | boolean | no  ...

request.description:
The properties an end user may change on an existing request: a comment, the solved flag, collaborators and the
organization. Every other request attribute is read-only once the request exists, and the properties accepted only on
create are not accepted here.

additional_collaborators.description:
Collaborators (CCs) to add to the request, as user ids, email addresses, or objects carrying a name and an email.
Existing collaborators are kept. Only applied when the account allows collaborators. At most 48 collaborators may
be sent in one call on accounts with CCs and followers enabled, and null is ignored

email.description: The email address of the collaborator

name.description: The name to use if a user has to be created for `email`

comment.description: The comment to add. Null and an empty object are both accepted and add no comment

anyOf.description:
The comment to add to the request. On Create Request the comment is mandatory and supplies the request's read-only
`description`. A comment carrying `uploads` but no text is rejected on both operations. Comments added through this
endpoint always take the publicity the account computes for the caller; an end user cannot choose it here.

body.description: The comment text, as Zendesk markdown. Takes precedence over `value`, but is overridden by `html_body` when both are sent. On create this becomes the request's `description`

html_body.description: The comment text as HTML. Takes precedence over both `body` and `value` whenever it is sent, and stores the comment in rich-text format

uploads.description:
One or more attachment upload tokens to attach to the comment. Blank tokens are discarded, and both a null and an
empty array are discarded entirely, leaving the comment with no new attachments. On an anonymous create the number
of attachments is capped by the account's anonymous attachment limit

value.description: A legacy alias for `body`, applied only when `body` is absent, and likewise overridden by `html_body`

email_ccs.description:
Email CCs to add to or remove from the request, up to 48 entries with `action: "put"` per call. Each entry is
applied on its own and CCs that are not listed are left untouched, so null and an empty array both leave the CC
list unchanged. On an account without CCs and followers enabled the `put` entries are still applied, as plain
collaborators; only `delete` entries need the feature

items.description: An email CC to add to, or remove from, a request.

action.description: "put" to add the email CC, "delete" to remove it. Defaults to "put", and any unrecognised value is also treated as "put"

user_email.description: The email address of the user to add or remove as an email CC. Used to look the user up when `user_id` is absent

user_id.description: The id of the user to add or remove as an email CC. Takes precedence over `user_email`

user_name.description: The name to use if a user has to be created for `user_email`

organization_id.description:
The id of the organization to associate the request with. Applied for the requester, who may always edit their own
request's properties. Unlike on create there is no silent substitution here: an organization the requester does not
belong to **fails the update** with a 422 and `organization_id is not a valid organization for the requester`.
Null is replaced by the requester's default organization, if they have one

safe_update.description: Set to true to make the update conditional on `updated_stamp` still matching the request's `updated_at`. Null is ignored

solved.description:
Set to true to solve the request. Only applied when the request is assigned to an agent, which the request's
read-only `can_be_solved_by_me` property reports. Null is ignored

system_metadata.description: Client and IP information to store as system metadata on the update's audit. Accepted from any caller but only applied for internal Zendesk services, and a null is ignored

client.description: The user agent to record against the update

ip_address.description: The IP address to record against the update

updated_stamp.description: The request's last known `updated_at`, used with `safe_update` to reject the update if the request has changed since. Null is ignored

via.description: The channel the update came through

anyOf.description:
Describes the channel the request came through. The channel is only recorded on the request when the account has the
agent-as-end-user anonymous via feature enabled, or when an internal Zendesk service records an LLM via; `source` is
always inspected to detect a help center submission, which changes whether collaborators may be set.

channel.description: The channel to record, either as a `via_id` or as a channel name. An unrecognised name is ignored and the request keeps its default channel

source.description: The via reference recorded against the request, for example the id of the ticket a follow-up came from. Send the help center via id here to identify a help center submission

rel.description: A relation name classifying the source

When brand separation is enabled, scopes user results to the specified brand.
This parameter applies only when the account has brand separation enabled
(`brand_user_separation_eap`). Non-user document types are unaffected.

Accepted values:

* "all" — apply no brand scoping.
* 0 — return only account-scoped (brand-less) end users; all agents and admins remain visible.
* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, return that
  brand's end users plus the agents with membership in that brand and all admins.
  If the brand's users are account-scoped, return the account-scoped end users, any end
  users still indexed with the brand, and all agents and admins. A brand id that does
  not exist on the account matches no users.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request, whether or not brand separation is enabled.

Omitting `brand_id` applies no brand scoping; this endpoint does not fall back to the
account's default brand_id behavior. Use the users search and autocomplete endpoints
for that fallback.

The query keyword forms (`query=type:user brand_id:{brand_id}` and `brand:{brand_id}`)
continue to work. They match the brand id as indexed on every document type, so agents
and admins match only through their brand memberships. When brand separation is enabled
and the brand's users are account-scoped, they also match every account-scoped end user,
and a negated keyword (`-brand_id:{brand_id}`) excludes those end users too.

Create Sharing Agreement. #### Allowed For

sharing_agreement.description: The writable attributes accepted when creating a sharing agreement.

allows_public_comments.description:
Whether the remote account may add public comments to the shared ticket and keep its status in
sync. When `false`, public comments arriving from the remote account are **discarded** rather
than imported — they are not stored as private comments — and ticket status is neither sent to
nor accepted from the remote account. Even when `true`, an account setting can separately
suppress a remote request to close the ticket. Defaults to `false` when omitted. Like
`sync_tags`, this value is only communicated to the remote account with the initial invitation
and cannot be changed later through the API.

remote_subdomain.description:
The subdomain of the Zendesk account you want to share tickets with. The account must already
exist — an unrecognized or blank subdomain is rejected, as is your own subdomain. This is the
only way to identify the remote party through this endpoint, so agreements created here are
always Zendesk-to-Zendesk and always outbound; agreements with Jira or another third party can
only be created in the admin interface. The new agreement is created with `status` `pending`
and an invitation is sent to the remote account, which must accept it before tickets can be
shared.

sync_custom_fields.description:
Whether custom field values are copied between the local ticket and its shared copy on the
remote account. Fields are matched by title, so a value is only applied on either side if a
ticket field with the same title exists there. Defaults to `false` when omitted. Like
`sync_tags`, this value is only communicated to the remote account with the initial invitation
and cannot be changed later through the API.

sync_tags.description:
Whether tags are copied between the local ticket and its shared copy on the remote account.
Defaults to `false` when omitted. This value is only communicated to the remote account with
the initial invitation, so it cannot be changed later through the API — only `status` is
updatable.

Show a Sharing Agreement. Returns a sharing agreement for your account.

actions.description:
Update a Sharing Agreement. Returns an updated sharing agreement. Only `status` is allowed to be updated.

#### Allowed For

* Admins

sharing_agreement_id.description: The ID of the sharing agreement

sharing_agreement.description:
The writable attributes accepted when updating a sharing agreement. Only `status` can be changed;
the sharing options chosen when the agreement was created are fixed for its lifetime. Sending an
empty object is accepted and changes nothing, though the agreement is re-validated on every request,
so the rejections described under `status` can apply even to a request that changes nothing.

status.description:
The state of the agreement. Use `accepted` to accept an invitation you have received, `declined`
to reject or cancel one, `inactive` to suspend an accepted agreement without deleting it, and
`accepted` again to resume a suspended one. A request that actually changes the status sends the
new state to the account on the other side of the agreement, unless the new status is
`ssl_error`; a request that leaves the status as it was sends nothing. Moving to `inactive`,
`failed`, `ssl_error` or `configuration_error` also emails every administrator on your account;
the other statuses do not.

Three transitions are rejected. Moving back to `accepted` is rejected unless Zendesk recorded
your own account as the one that suspended the agreement, which it does only for an `accepted`
to `inactive` change made on your side — so an agreement the *other* account suspended cannot be
resumed from here. Moving to `pending` or `accepted` is rejected while you hold another accepted
agreement with the same remote URL in the same direction. Moving to anything other than
`inactive` or `declined` is rejected when the agreement's remote URL has come to point back at
your own account, which can happen after a subdomain change.

`failed`, `ssl_error` and `configuration_error` describe communication problems and are normally
set by Zendesk rather than by a client, but they are accepted here.

Note that `declined` set through this endpoint marks the agreement declined without deleting it
or its shared tickets — use the delete endpoint for that.

A blank value is accepted and leaves the status unchanged. `null` and an empty string are both
listed in the enum for that reason; a whitespace-only string such as `" "` behaves the same way
but cannot be enumerated. Omitting the property has the same effect. An unrecognized status name
is rejected.

holds a given value. Requires the account's native conditional fields feature; without it the `agent_conditions`
array is silently ignored.

actions.name: reorder_ticket_forms
actions.description:
Reorder Ticket Forms. #### Allowed For
* Admins

#### Request Parameters

You can pass in the following parameter in the payload:

| Name                | Type   | Comment
| ------------------- | ------ | --------
| ticket_form_ids     | array  | An array of ticket form ids. Example: "[2, 23, 46, 50]"

ticket_form_ids.description:
The IDs of the ticket forms in their new order, where the first ID becomes position 0. The list must name every
form of a single form type on the account — a partial list, or a mix of standard and service catalog form IDs,
is rejected

actions.name: get_ticket_forms_show_many
actions.description:
Show Many Ticket Forms. Takes an `ids` query parameter that accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 ticket form ids. This endpoint is used primarily by the [mobile SDK](/documentation/classic-web-widget-sdks/) and the [Web Widget](/api-reference/widget/introduction/).

#### Allowed For

* Anyone

ids.description: IDs of the ticket forms to be shown

include_boundary_indicators.description:
When true, includes `has_more` indicator in the cursor pagination response meta.

Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).

include_item_cursors.description:
When true, includes cursor values for each item in the cursor pagination response.

Only valid with cursor pagination (page[size], page[after], page[before]).

active.description: true returns active ticket forms; false returns inactive ticket forms. If not present, returns both

end_user_visible.description: true returns ticket forms where `end_user_visible`; false returns ticket forms that are not end-user visible. If not present, returns both

fallback_to_default.description: true returns the default ticket form when the criteria defined by the parameters results in a set without active and end-user visible ticket forms

associated_to_brand.description: true returns the ticket forms of the brand specified by the url's subdomain

actions.name: list_ticket_metrics
actions.description:
List Ticket Metrics. Returns a list of tickets with their metrics.

Tickets are ordered chronologically by created date, from newest to oldest.
The last ticket listed may not be the absolute oldest ticket in your account
due to ticket archiving.

Archived tickets are not included in the response. See
[About archived tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408887617050) in
Zendesk help.

#### Pagination

- Cursor pagination (recommended)
- Offset pagination

See [Pagination](/api-reference/introduction/pagination/).

Returns a maximum of 100 records per page.


#### Allowed For

* Agents

after.description: Cursor token for fetching next page

before.description: Cursor token for fetching previous page

page.description:
Cursor-based pagination parameters (JSON:API style).

Supports nested parameters:
- `page[size]` - Number of records per page (default varies by endpoint, typically 100)
- `page[after]` - Cursor token to fetch records after this position
- `page[before]` - Cursor token to fetch records before this position

Example: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`

sort.description:
Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order.

When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering.

Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`

actions.name: delete_zendesk_ticket
actions.description:
Delete Ticket. #### Allowed For

* Admins
* Agents with permission to delete tickets

Agent delete permissions are set in Support. See
[Deleting tickets](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408883872538)
in the Support Help Center.

#### Ticket deletion rate limit

You can delete 400 tickets every 1 minute using this endpoint.
The rate limiting mechanism behaves as described in
[Rate limits](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/) in the API introduction.
Zendesk recommends that you obey the Retry-After header values.
To delete many tickets, you may use [Bulk Delete Tickets](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#bulk-delete-tickets).

actions.description:
Create a Satisfaction Rating. Creates a CSAT rating for a solved ticket, or for a ticket that was previously
solved and then reopened.

Only the end user listed as the ticket requester can create a satisfaction rating for the ticket.

Only "good" and "bad" are valid values for the score when creating a rating. Other states, like "offered", are not valid and will result in a 422 error.

The end user must be a verified user.

A non-empty comment upgrades the score stored on the ticket from "good" to "good_with_comment" or from "bad" to "bad_with_comment", although the `score` in the response still reads "good" or "bad"

reason_code.description: The reason code for a negative rating. See [Reason codes](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/satisfaction_reasons/#reason-codes) in the Satisfaction Reasons API. **This property is only accepted on accounts that have satisfaction reasons enabled**; on any other account the property is silently dropped and the rating is created without it, with a success response and no error. It also only takes effect on a "bad" score — a "good" score resets the reason to the default 0 ("no reason"). An explicit `null` is accepted and ignored, preserving any reason code already recorded on the ticket

score.description: The rating. Only "good" and "bad" create a rating: the parameter filter accepts the full satisfaction-score vocabulary used by the List Satisfaction Ratings `score` filter ("offered", "unoffered", "received", "good_with_comment" and so on), but any value other than "good" or "bad" is mapped to no score and the request then fails validation with a 422 rather than a 400

`false` has the same effect as omitting the property or sending `null`: no collision
check is performed. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See [Protecting against
ticket update collisions](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#protecting-against-ticket-update-collisions)

A ticket is considered active when it's open and the messaging session is still in progress.

replacement, and null is treated the same as `[]`: sending either alongside `restrict_access_by_role: true` leaves
