actions.name: update_user_field
actions.description:
Update User Field. #### Updating a Dropdown (Tagger) or Multiselect Field

Dropdown and multiselect fields return an array of `custom_field_options` which specify the name, value, and order of the list of dropdown or multiselect options.
Understand the following behavior when updating a dropdown or multiselect field:

- All options must be passed on update. Options that are not passed will be removed. As a result, these values will be removed from any organizations.
- To create a new option, pass a null `id` along with `name` and `value`.
- To update an existing option, pass its `id` along with `name` and `value`.
- To re-order an option, reposition it in the `custom_field_options` array ...

user_field_id.description: The ID or key of the user field

user_field.description:
The writable attributes accepted when updating a user field. The field's `type`, `key`, and
`relationship_target_type` cannot be changed after creation, so none of them is listed here. `type` and
`relationship_target_type` are discarded if sent; sending a `key` different from the field's current key fails
validation.

active.description:
Whether this field is available. Sending null does not leave the field unchanged: it reactivates the field, because
a nil `is_active` is defaulted back to `true`.

custom_field_options.description:
For `dropdown`, `tagger`, and `multiselect` fields only. Sending it for any other field type fails with an
`Invalid` error on the request.

**Destructive:** this array is a full replacement, not a patch. Every existing option you want to keep must be
present in every update request. Any option you omit is deleted, and those values are removed from the users that
held them. Passing an empty array deletes every option on the field. Omitting the `custom_field_options` key
entirely leaves the options untouched, so a partial update must omit the key rather than send a partial list.

Every entry must include an `id`: supply an existing option's `id` to update it in place, or a null or empty `id`
to add a new option. An entry with no `id` key at all is rejected. The array order determines each option's
position.

Null and `[]` are **not** interchangeable here. `custom_field_options: null` is accepted and ignored, leaving the
options untouched — it is the same as omitting the key. `custom_field_options: []` deletes every option on the
field and returns a 200. Send null, or omit the key, if you mean "leave the options alone".

An option for a `dropdown`, `tagger`, or `multiselect` custom user field, as supplied when updating the field. The
`id` key must always be present.

id.description:
The id of an existing option to update in place. To add a new option, send null or an empty string. The key
itself is mandatory on every entry: an option with no `id` key is rejected with a `BlankValue` error.

name.description: The presentation name of the option. Must not be blank. Required when adding a new option

raw_name.description:
The dynamic content placeholder for the option's name. See [Dynamic Content](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/dynamic_content/).
When supplied, this value is written to `name` and any `name` sent alongside it is discarded. Sending null is
accepted and discarded: `name` is left as sent.

value.description:
The tag value applied to the user when the option is selected. Must be unique across the account's field options.
Required when adding a new option; when updating an existing option by `id`, omitting it leaves the current value
unchanged.

When adding an option whose `value` matches one that was previously deleted, the deleted option is restored
instead. That match is case-sensitive, so a value differing only in case does not restore the old option.

description.description:
User-defined description of this field's purpose. Sending null does not clear it: the field's current `title` is
written into `description` instead.

permissions.description:
Restricts which agent roles can read and update this field's values. Only honored on accounts with the
`permissions_custom_user_fields` feature enabled; on all other accounts the key is accepted and silently ignored.
Sending null is equivalent to omitting the key and leaves any existing permissions untouched.

restrict_access_by_role.description:
Whether access to this field's values is restricted to the roles listed in `roles`. When false, all agents retain
access. Null is treated as false, so sending null lifts the restriction rather than leaving it unchanged.

roles.description:
The custom agent roles granted access to this field, and the scopes each is granted. This list is a full
replacement, and null is treated the same as `[]`: sending either alongside `restrict_access_by_role: true` leaves
only the account's admin roles with access and drops every other role's grant.

items.description: A custom agent role's access to a user field's values.

role_id.description: The id of the custom agent role

scopes.description:
The scopes granted to the role. `["update"]` on its own is rejected with a 400, because update access requires read
access. `["read"]` on its own is only honored on accounts with the `permissions_custom_user_fields_read_only_release`
feature enabled; without it, the API silently upgrades the role to `["read", "update"]`.

position.description:
Ordering of the field relative to other fields. Unlike on create, this writes the field's position directly without
shifting its siblings, so it can leave two fields sharing a position. Use Reorder User Field to reposition a field
within the account's ordering.

null is accepted and discarded: `description` is left as sent, or unchanged if no `description` was sent.

actions.description:
Create or Update a User Field Option. Creates a new option or updates an existing option for the given drop-down user field.

To update an option, include the id of the option in the `custom_field_option` object. Example: `{"custom_field_option": {"id": 10002, "name": "Pineapples", ... }`. If an option exists for the given ID, the option will be updated. Otherwise, a new option will be created.

#### Response

Returns one of the following status codes:

- 200 with `Location: /api/v2/user_fields/{user_field_id}/options` if the user field option already exists in the database
- 201 with `Location: /api/v2/user_fields/{user_field_id}/options` if the user field option is new

A single option for a `dropdown` user field, created or updated in place. Fields created with `type: tagger` are
dropdown fields and are also supported. `multiselect` fields are not: this endpoint returns 404 for them, and their
options must be managed through the `custom_field_options` array on Update User Field.

Supplying `id` updates that option. When `id` is omitted or null, the API looks up an option on the field with the
same `value`, whether that option is active or previously deleted. If one is found it is updated in place, restored if
it had been deleted, and the response is a 200 rather than a 201 — so reusing an existing `value` silently mutates
that option instead of creating a new one. Otherwise a new option is created.

unchanged.

When brand separation is enabled, scopes the listing to users belonging to
the specified brand. Only applicable when the account has brand separation enabled.

Accepted values:

* "all" — return all users across all brands (no brand filtering applied).
* 0 — return only account-scoped (brand-less) end users plus all agents and admins.
* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, return
  end users belonging to that brand plus the agents with membership in
  that brand and all admins. If the brand does not have user separation
  enabled, the request falls back to account scope (0).

If `brand_id` is omitted, the account's `brand_user_separation_scope_query_default`
[brand setting](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/account_settings/#brands)

actions.name: create_user_identity
actions.description:
Create Identity. Adds an identity to a user's profile. An agent can add an identity to any user profile.

Supported identity types:

| Type             | Example |
| ---------------- | ------- |
| email            | `{ "type" : "email", "value" : "someone@example.com" }` |
| twitter          | `{ "type" : "twitter", "value" : "screen_name" }` |
| facebook         | `{ "type" : "facebook", "value" : "855769377321" }` |
| google           | `{ "type" : "google", "value" : "example@gmail.com" }` |
| agent_forwarding | `{ "type" : "agent_forwarding", "value" : "+1 555-123-4567" }` |
| phone_number     | `{ "type" : "phone_number", "value" : "+1 555-123-4567" }` |

To create an identity withou...

brand_id.description:
When the account has multiple active brands, sets the active brand context
for the created identity. Used to scope verification emails to the correct brand.

auto_ownership.description: When true, creates the email identity as "owned", or as "shared" if another user owns the address. See [Shared email](/api-reference/ticketing/users/user_identities/#shared-email).

ownership.description: Sets the email identity to "owned" or "shared". Defaults to "owned". See [Shared email](/api-reference/ticketing/users/user_identities/#shared-email).

primary.description:
Makes the new identity the primary one. null is accepted and ignored. Only takes effect for `email` identities. For a verified
email identity (`verified: true` or `verification_method: low`) the identity becomes primary
immediately; for an unverified one the promotion is deferred - the verification email link carries
`make_primary=true`, so the identity becomes primary (and the former primary is removed) when the
recipient verifies. Ignored for non-email identity types, including `google`.

To promote an identity that already exists, use the
[Make Identity Primary](#make-identity-primary) endpoint instead.

skip_verify_email.description:
Suppresses the verification or welcome email for the new identity. null is accepted and treated
exactly like `false`. Only effective when an agent
creates an identity for a different user - it is ignored when adding an identity to your own
profile.

type.description:
The type of identity to create.

Only the types listed here can be created through this endpoint. The remaining identity types
(`any_channel`, `foreign`, `sdk`, `microsoft`) are created by internal systems only, and a request
for one of them is rejected with a `400`. The deprecated `phone` alias is likewise rejected
here - use `phone_number`.

`messaging` and `slack` back internal channel integrations. `slack` additionally requires the
Slack identity feature to be enabled on the account.

value.description:
The identifier for this identity. An email address for `email` and `google`, the screen name for
`twitter`, the Facebook user id for `facebook`, and an E.164 phone number for `phone_number` and
`agent_forwarding`. Phone numbers are validated unless the account has phone number validation
turned off.

verification_method.description:
The verification state to create the identity with. `low` creates a verified identity and
suppresses the verification email. Only `none` and `low` are accepted here; the higher methods
(`sso`, `embed`, `full`) are set by the corresponding authentication flows.

Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor
for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is
always created unverified and a verification email is sent.

null is accepted and treated exactly like `none`. Because this property wins over `verified`,
sending `verified: true` alongside `verification_method: null` creates an unverified identity.

verified.description:
Creates the identity already verified, equivalent to `verification_method: low`. Deprecated - use
`verification_method` instead. Ignored when `verification_method` is also sent - that property
wins. null is accepted and treated exactly like `false`.

Has no effect for `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding` identities, which are always verified, nor
for `slack`. Also ignored when creating an email identity (including `google`) for the account owner: that identity is
always created unverified and a verification email is sent.

actions.name: update_users_identity
actions.description:
Update Identity. This endpoint allows you to:

* Set the specified identity as verified (by setting `verified` to "true" or `verification_method` to "low")
* Unverify a verified identity (by setting `verified` to "false" or `verification_method` to "none")
* Update the `value` property of the specified identity

You can't change an identity's `primary` attribute with this endpoint. You must use the [Make Identity Primary](#make-identity-primary) endpoint instead.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

user_identity_id.description: The ID of the user identity

identity.description:
The attributes to change. An explicit null is accepted and is a complete no-op: the whole update
branch is skipped, so unlike `{}` it does not unverify and re-mail a non-primary email identity of
the account owner.

auto_ownership.description: When true, sets the email identity to "owned", or to "shared" if another user owns the address. See [Shared email](/api-reference/ticketing/users/user_identities/#shared-email).

deliverable_state.description: Clears the undeliverable state of an email identity, so that Zendesk resumes sending to it. `deliverable` is the only value that has any effect, and only on an `email` identity that is currently undeliverable. Every other value, including null, is ignored.

ownership.description: Sets the email identity to "owned" or "shared". See [Shared email](/api-reference/ticketing/users/user_identities/#shared-email).

value.description:
The new identifier for this identity.

Changing the value resets `verification_method` to `none`, so the identity becomes unverified
unless the same request also sets `verified` or `verification_method`.

null is accepted and ignored - the current value is kept. It does not clear the value.

verification_method.description:
Verifies (`low`) or unverifies (`none`) the identity. Only `none` and `low` are accepted here; the
higher methods (`sso`, `embed`, `full`) are set by the corresponding authentication flows.

Ignored for identities that belong to the account owner. `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding`
identities are re-verified on every save, so `none` has no effect on them.

null is **not** ignored here: it is treated like `none` and unverifies the identity. Because this
property wins over `verified`, sending `verified: true` alongside `verification_method: null`
unverifies it.

verified.description:
Verifies (`true`) or unverifies (`false`) the identity. null is **not** ignored here: it is
treated like `false` and unverifies the identity. Equivalent to setting
`verification_method` to `low` or `none`. Deprecated - use `verification_method` instead. Ignored
when `verification_method` is also sent - that property wins.

Ignored for identities that belong to the account owner. `phone_number` and `agent_forwarding`
identities are re-verified on every save, so they cannot be unverified through this endpoint.

The ID of the organization to assign the user to. The organization must belong to the same account as

* If this is the user's first organization membership, it is created as the default, which also sets
  the user's `organization_id`, and every unclosed ticket requested by the user is reassigned to this
  organization.

  memberships are **deleted**, and the user's unclosed requested tickets that belonged to those
  removed organizations move to the user's new default organization — or have their organization
  cleared, if the account has the `unset_ticket_org_when_removing_default_user_org` feature. Tickets
  the user has in other organizations are left alone.
* Returns a 422 if the user is already at the account's `max_organization_memberships_per_user` limit
  (300 by default).

tags.description:
An array of tag strings, or a single string. In either form each value is split
on whitespace and on `,` `;` `|` `(` `)`, then stripped of special characters,
downcased and de-duplicated. **`null` is destructive**: it replaces the stored tags with
nothing, clearing every tag. An empty array, an empty string and omitting the property
entirely all do the same. Clearing every tag is the only thing `null` can mean here

safe_update.description:
Write only. When `true`, protects against ticket update collisions. Requires
`updated_stamp`; sending `safe_update` without it returns a `409` on every resource.
`false` has the same effect as omitting the property or sending `null`: no collision
check is performed. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See [Protecting against
ticket update collisions](/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/#protecting-against-ticket-update-collisions)

tags.description:
The tags to add to the ones already applied. An array of tag strings, or a single
string. In either form each value is split on whitespace and on `,` `;` `|` `(` `)`,
then stripped of special characters, downcased and de-duplicated. `null`, an empty array,
an empty string and omitting the property are all accepted and leave the existing tags
unchanged. Unlike the Set Tags operation, nothing here can clear a tag

updated_stamp.description:
Write only. The resource's last known `updated_at`. The update is applied only if it
still matches, otherwise the request returns a `409`. `null` has the same effect as
omitting the property: it is ignored unless `safe_update` is set, in which case the
request returns a `409`. Only affects the outcome for tickets. See the `safe_update`
property

via.description: Write only. `null` is accepted and treated as omitted. Only affects the outcome for tickets

author_zrn.description:
Write only. The Zendesk Resource Name (ZRN) of the actor on whose behalf the
update is made, recorded on the audit. At most 100 characters and must be a
valid ZRN. Only affects the outcome for tickets

channel.description:
The channel to attribute the update to. Defaults to `web_service` when unset,
`null` or unrecognized

Autocomplete Users. Returns an array of users whose name starts with the value specified in the `name` parameter.
It only returns users with no foreign identities.

#### Allowed For

* Agents

name.description: The name to search for the user. You must specify either `name` or `phone`.

phone.description: The phone number to search for the user. You must specify either `name` or `phone`.

filter.description: Filter to apply to autocomplete results.

field_id.description:
The id of a lookup relationship field.  The type of field is determined
by the `source` param

source.description:
If a `field_id` is provided, this specifies the type of the field.
For example, if the field is on a "zen:user", it references a field on a user

include.description:
Sideloads to include in the response. Accepts a comma-separated list of values.
See [Sideloading](/documentation/api-basics/working-with-data/side_loading/#supported-endpoints).

per_page.description: Number of results to return.

brand_id.description:
When brand separation is enabled, scopes the autocomplete results to users
belonging to the specified brand. Only applicable when the account has brand separation enabled.

Accepted values:

* "all" — search all users across all brands (no brand filtering applied).
* 0 — restrict the autocomplete results to account-scoped (brand-less) users only.
* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, autocomplete
  returns only end users belonging to that brand. Agents and admins are not included
  in the results when filtering by a specific brand. If the brand does not have user
  separation enabled, the request falls back to account scope (0).

If `brand_id` is omitted, the account's `brand_user_separation_scope_query_default`
[brand setting](/api-reference/ticketing/account-configuration/account_settings/#brands)
decides the scope. If it's set to `"error"`, the request is rejected with `400 Bad Request`.
Agent Workspace, other signed-in Zendesk sessions and internal Zendesk requests always use `all`. The resolved
scope is returned in the `X-Zendesk-Brand-Id-Scope-Resolved` response header.

The response includes a `refreshed_at` property in a `count` object that contains a timestamp indicating when the count was last updated.

**Note**: When the count exceeds 100,000, the `refreshed_at` property may occasionally be null.

the specified brand. Only applicable when the account has brand separation enabled.

Accepted values:

* "all" — count all users across all brands (no brand filtering applied).
* 0 — count only account-scoped (brand-less) end users plus all agents and admins.

  that brand and all admins. If the brand does not have user separation

scope is returned in the `X-Zendesk-Brand-Id-Scope-Resolved` response header.

actions.name: delete_users_destroy_many
actions.description:
Bulk Delete Users. Accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 user ids.

The request takes an `ids` or an `external_ids` query parameter.

#### Allowed for

* Admins

#### Response

This endpoint returns a `job_status` [JSON object](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#json-format) and queues a background job to do the work. Use the [Show Job Status](/api-reference/ticketing/ticket-management/job_statuses/#show-job-status) endpoint to check for the job's completion. Only a certain number of jobs can be queued or running at the same time. See [Job limit](/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/#job-limit) for more information.

ids.description: Id of the users to delete. Comma separated

external_ids.description: External Id of the users to delete. Comma separated

brand_id.description:
Scopes the deletion of users matched by `external_ids` to a specific brand
or to account-scoped (brand-less) users. Only applicable when the account
has brand separation enabled (`brand_user_separation_eap`); ignored
otherwise so existing numeric callers continue to behave as before.

Accepted values:

* `0` — restrict the lookup to account-scoped (brand-less) users only.
* A numeric brand id — restrict to that brand. Brands without
  `user_separation` enabled collapse to account scope (`0`).

Rejected with `400 Bad Request`:

* `all` — cross-brand deletion is not supported on this endpoint.
* Any other non-numeric string.
* A numeric brand id that does not exist on the account.

actions.name: update_many_views
actions.description:
Update Many Views. #### Allowed For

* Agents

#### Request Parameters

The PUT request expects a `views` object that lists the views to update.

Each view may have the following properties:

| Name     | Mandatory | Description
| -------- | --------- | -----------
| id       | yes       | The ID of the view to update
| position | no        | The new position of the view
| active   | no        | The active status of the view (true or false)

#### Example Request Body

```js
{
  "views": [
    {"id": 25, "position": 3},
    {"id": 23, "position": 5},
    {"id": 27, "position": 9},
    {"id": 22, "position": 7}
  ]
}
```

actions.description: Update Article.

article_id.description: The unique ID of the article

article.description:
Only the properties documented here are applied to the article. Any other
key does not change the article.

author_id.description:
The id of the user to set as the article's author. `null`, `false`, or
omission is a no-op: the author is left unchanged. There is no way to
clear the author via this property.

block_attachment_ids.description:
The full set of block (non-inline) attachment ids for this article; the
previous set is entirely replaced by the given set. Omit the property to
leave block attachments unchanged; send `[]` to detach every block
attachment. Do not send `null` — sending it alone is rejected with a
400 (a `TypeError` from the same internal concatenation, but this time
caught by the controller). Sending it together with an explicit
`inline_attachment_ids: null` still 500s, because `inline_attachment_ids`
is evaluated first.

comments_disabled.description:
True if comments are disabled; false otherwise. `null` is accepted and
treated the same as `false` (enables comments) — it is not a no-op.

content_tag_ids.description:
The full set of content tag ids attached to this article; the previous
set is entirely replaced by the given set. `null` and `[]` are
equivalent and both remove every content tag. Omit the property to
leave content tags unchanged. Only available on certain plans; ignored
otherwise.

inline_attachment_ids.description:
The full set of inline attachment ids for this article; the previous
set is entirely replaced by the given set. Omit the property to leave
inline attachments unchanged; send `[]` to detach every inline
attachment. Do not send `null` — it currently causes an uncaught 500
(`nil` is on the left side of an internal array concatenation with
`block_attachment_ids`, so `NoMethodError` is raised and not rescued).

label_names.description:
An array of label names associated with this article. Only available on
certain plans; ignored otherwise. Omit the property to leave labels
unchanged; send `[]` to remove every label. Do not send `null` — it is
rejected with a 400 (must be an array of strings).

owner.description:
Assigns ownership of the article. Set to `null` to unassign ownership.
When present, both `id` and `type` are required together — a partial
object (e.g. `type` without `id`) is rejected with a 500, not a 400, so
always send both keys or omit the property entirely. Only takes effect
when the account has the article-owner feature; otherwise the property
is silently ignored.

id.description: The id of the owning user or group.

type.description: Whether `id` refers to a user or a group.

permission_group_id.description:
The id of the permission group which defines who can edit and publish
this article. `null`, `false`, or omission is a no-op: the permission
group is left unchanged.

position.description:
The position of this article in the article list. `0` is a valid
position and is applied. `null`, `false`, or omission leaves the
position unchanged.

promoted.description:
True if this article is promoted; false otherwise. `null` is accepted
and treated the same as `false` (demotes the article) — it is not a
no-op.

section_id.description:
The id of the section to move the article into. `null`, `false`, or
omission is a no-op: the section is left unchanged.

source_locale.description:
The locale to make the source (default) translation of the article.
Do not send `null` — it currently causes a 500.

theme.description:
The identifier of an alternate template assigned to this article. Set
to `null` to remove the alternate-template assignment and revert the
article to the default template for its type.

user_segment_id.description:
The id of the user segment which defines who can see this article.
Set to `null` to make the article visible to everyone (unrestrict
viewing). Omit to leave the current restriction unchanged. Only one of
`user_segment_id` or `user_segment_ids` may be supplied in the same
request; supplying both is rejected with a 400.

user_segment_ids.description:
List of user segment ids which define who can view this article. `null`
and `[]` are equivalent and both unrestrict viewing (make the article
visible to everyone). Omit to leave the current restriction unchanged.
For Enterprise plans this may contain more than one id. Only one of
`user_segment_id` or `user_segment_ids` may be supplied in the same
request; supplying both is rejected with a 400.

actions.name: show_phone_number
actions.description:
Show Phone Number. Retrieves a phone number.

#### Including additional information

Use the `include` query parameter to retrieve additional information about a phone number. The parameter accepts the following values:

- all_greetings
- all_groups
- all_schedules
- ivrs
- settings

For example, to retrieve a phone number's settings, use `?include=settings`.  The response includes a `settings` child object in the `phone_number` object. For returned `settings` properties, see [Settings JSON Format](#settings-json-format).

Use commas to separate multiple values. Example:`?include=settings,ivrs,all_groups`.

#### Allowed For
- Agents

include.description: Parameter to include additional information

actions.name: update_phone_number
actions.description:
Update Phone Number. Updates an existing phone number.

#### Including additional information

Use the `include` query parameter to update additional information about a phone number. The parameter accepts the following values:

- all_greetings
- all_groups
- all_schedules
- ivrs
- settings

For example, to update a phone number's settings, use `?include=settings` and include a `settings` child object in the request body's `phone_number` object. For supported `settings` properties, see [Settings JSON Format](#settings-json-format).

Use commas to separate multiple values. Example:`?include=settings,ivrs,all_groups`.
